study_type: Exploratory cross-cohort video-phenotyping development and external validation
title: Simultaneous hyperkinetic movement disorders phenotyping: a cross-cohort pediatric transfer study using routine videos, markerless pose estimation and a tabular foundation model
population: Single-center adult movement-disorder development cohort; independent routine-video pediatric cohort with monogenic combined movement disorders. Neither is a defined persistent-severe-adult Tourette cohort.
sampling_unit_caution: The 125 labeled video-derived files arise from the same 25 people: 50 full-examination labels from two raters plus 75 condition-specific files. Neither files nor the 56 correlated held-out person-by-phenotype decisions are independent participant counts.
comparator: Generic uncalibrated decision rule versus locally calibrated aggregation/thresholds, with the shared model fixed; reference labels from five clinicians.
exposure: Routine clinical videos processed with pose estimation, kinematic features and a pretrained tabular model; no clinical treatment assigned.
outcomes: Eight movement-phenotype classifications, Hamming accuracy and Jaccard overlap; not symptoms, pain, function, remission or clinical benefit.
follow_up: No prospective clinical-outcome or treatment-withdrawal follow-up established.
reported_aggregate_results: Across seven held-out pediatric participants under majority labels, Hamming accuracy increased .804 to .839 and Jaccard .548 to .633 after calibration. False positives increased 2 to 5. These are overall multi-phenotype metrics, not tic-specific sensitivity.
tic_specific_result: No consensus-positive tics in the external cohort, including the seven held-out participants. Tic sensitivity has a zero positive-case denominator and is not estimable, not 0% or 100%. Correct negative calls do not establish detection of actual tics.
negative_and_contradictory_evidence: Under unanimous main-label rules, calibrated Jaccard was lower than baseline (.512 versus .655). Myoclonus was not recovered in held-out positives. Performance depends on reference-label construction and calibration subset; some apparent accuracy comes from invariant labels.
uncertainty: Seven held-out people, clinician-selected calibration subset, reference disagreement and domain shift; no raw-data/code reanalysis or cluster-aware uncertainty reconstruction. Reported decision-level intervals are not treated as person-level clinical precision.
prespecification: Methods describe grouped development cross-validation and separated calibration/held-out people; preregistration and independent code verification not established.
attrition_missingness: Complete recruitment/exclusion and recording-failure flow not independently established. Uncertain training labels were excluded for the relevant phenotype; restrictive reference definitions omit ambiguous labels.
adverse_events: No therapeutic safety or patient-benefit inference from this observational methods study.
funding_conflicts: Dystonia Medical Research Foundation Canada support; authors report no commercial/financial conflicts; two authors disclose Frontiers editorial-board roles.
applicability: Adjacent measurement evidence only. It does not validate tic-positive pediatric sensitivity, adult Tourette deployment, severe adult burden measurement, symptom monitoring or treatment selection.
related_cohorts: The development cohort relates to earlier CODY-SAMP/video work cited by the authors; this is not independent replication of every earlier training report. Exact cross-report overlap not fully audited.
claim_supported: A small multi-phenotype transfer experiment and explicit lack of external tic-positive sensitivity evidence.
claim_not_supported: Validated tic detection, clinical-grade diagnostic reliability, prospective tic prediction, efficacy, disease modification or cure.
full_text_status: Publisher HTML and lawful official PMC XML inspected transiently for selected methods, aggregate results and disclosures; CC BY 4.0 metadata verified. No full paper, patient images, videos, case narratives or individual result rows retained.
correction_retraction_check: No linked correction/retraction in retrieved PubMed metadata; not exhaustive publisher/Crossmark clearance.
reviewer: AI-assisted source extraction; not independent clinical peer review.
next_verification_task: Require an external tic-positive cohort with participant-level split, clinically relevant reference labels, tic-specific denominators and uncertainty before promoting tic-detection claims. No patient data request or reanalysis authorized.
